elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted subparagraph: "Teleglobe USA Inc. may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time..." In this multiparty consortium there are no Order Forms; termination of our participation is the functional full exit for us, and the right is unconditional (no cause, no consent of other Parties, opened by "In addition to Subparagraph 18.1" so 18.1's end-of-term restriction does not bite).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties" — exactly the 30-day written-notice anchor, no additional condition or approval step.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "the other Parties shall refund to Teleglobe USA Inc., pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it for the period after the effective date of such termination" — express "pro rata" wording (not merely a post-termination-period refund), running against the counterparties.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met and left untouched: 18.1 permits a Party to terminate its participation only "at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" on one year's notice, and 18.2 allows mid-Initial-Period termination only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties", so the counterparties have no unilateral mid-term convenience exit. The new right is expressly reserved to Teleglobe USA Inc. alone and does not enlarge their rights.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is "not less than thirty (30) days", which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band. Not a defect: the preferred (30-day) position is stronger for us and is fully met, so the fallback band is not the operative target.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the inserted clause imposes no early-termination fee or exit charge, and 18.5's no-capital-cost-credit rule is keyed only to "Subparagraph 18.1" terminations, so it does not attach to the new right. A zero fee satisfies a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 ties any other Party's exit to "the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; there is no mid-term unilateral right (18.2 requires unanimous written agreement).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice", exceeding the 90-day floor.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single inserted subparagraph supplies the Customer-side convenience right, the 30-day written-notice anchor and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, while the pre-existing 18.1/18.2 structure already denies the other Parties any mid-Initial-Period convenience exit.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical miss only: the drafter used the named party "Teleglobe USA Inc." rather than the alias "Customer", but the operative grant is an unconditional Customer election to terminate without cause, i.e. a convenience right.

Minimality holds: nothing favourable was deleted, no words outside the checklist were touched, the model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists), and no survival tail, expense allocation or procedural boilerplate was added. For a missing clause, an all-new but concise insertion can still be minimal.

Intent is preserved: the opening "In addition to Subparagraph 18.1" resolves the tension with 18.1's end-of-term-only language without a broad notwithstanding override, and because the new right sits outside 18.1 the retained 18.5 capital-cost rule and 18.7 continuing-liability tail (both expressly keyed to Subparagraph 18.1) remain intact and non-contradictory. No dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created.

Drafting hygiene only, not an element defect: the rendered insertion carries no subparagraph number even though the comment calls it "18.8" — number it in the executed redline to avoid a citation gap. Also confirm on the signature page that Teleglobe USA Inc. is the client entity, since the clause names a party rather than a defined "Customer".

Note in the rationale that the refund covers "any amounts prepaid" rather than "prepaid fees"; that is broader in our favour and needs no change, but expect the counterparty to try to narrow it to fees.
